papers.title: ROOF: Robustness-Oriented Optimal Factorization for Fluorescence Crosstalk Correction
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Fluorescence bleed-through (spectral crosstalk) compromises the accuracy of signal interpretation, quantification, and visualization in multi-band fluorescence microscopy. Existing correction methods rely either on experimental calibration or blind spectral unmixing, but often suffer from limited robustness to biological variability, overcorrection artifacts, or the need for manual parameter tuning. We propose ROOF (Robustness-Oriented Optimal Factorization), a semi-blind framework that unifies calibration-based modeling with data-driven spectral unmixing. It formulates crosstalk correction as a diagonally normalized nonnegative matrix factorization problem regularized by a reference crosstalk matrix obtained from single-labeled control samples. The regularization parameter is estimated automatically via maximum likelihood, eliminating manual tuning while adapting to specimen-specific variations. Results Experiments on synthetic and real four-band fluorescence images demonstrate that ROOF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art crosstalk correction methods. ROOF achieves higher correction accuracy, suppresses overcorrection artifacts, preserves biologically meaningful fluorescence colocalization, and is computationally efficient. These results highlight ROOF’s robustness, efficiency, and practical value for reliable quantitative fluorescence imaging. Availability and implementation The codes are available at https://github.com/baobabking/ROOF with
papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Fluorescence bleed-through (spectral crosstalk) compromises the accuracy of signal interpretation, quantification, and visualization in multi-band fluorescence microscopy. Existing correction methods rely either on experimental calibration or blind spectral unmixing, but often suffer from limited robustness to biological variability, overcorrection artifacts, or the need for manual parameter tuning. We propose ROOF (Robustness-Oriented Optimal Factorization), a semi-blind framework that unifies calibration-based modeling with data-driven spectral unmixing. It formulates crosstalk correction as a diagonally normalized nonnegative matrix factorization problem regularized by a reference crosstalk matrix obtained from single-labeled control samples. The regularization parameter is estimated automatically via maximum likelihood, eliminating manual tuning while adapting to specimen-specific variations.

RESULTS: Experiments on synthetic and real four-band fluorescence images demonstrate that ROOF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art crosstalk correction methods. ROOF achieves higher correction accuracy, suppresses overcorrection artifacts, preserves biologically meaningful fluorescence colocalization, and is computationally efficient. These results highlight ROOF's robustness, efficiency, and practical value for reliable quantitative fluorescence imaging.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The codes are available at https://github.com/baobabking/ROOF with DOI:10.5281/zenodo.21872937.

papers.llm_research_question_zh: 荧光渗透（光谱串扰）会影响多波段荧光显微镜中信号解释、定量和可视化的准确性。
llm_highlights_zh: 现有的校正方法依赖于实验校准或盲光谱分离，但通常会受到对生物变异性、过度校正伪影或需要手动参数调整的鲁棒性有限的影响。
我们提出了 ROOF（面向稳健性的最佳分解），这是一种半盲框架，它将基于校准的建模与数据驱动的光谱分解相结合。
它将串扰校正公式化为对角归一化非负矩阵分解问题，并通过从单标记控制样本获得的参考串扰矩阵进行正则化。
papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 荧光渗透（光谱串扰）会影响多波段荧光显微镜中信号解释、定量和可视化的准确性。现有的校正方法依赖于实验校准或盲光谱分离，但通常会受到对生物变异性、过度校正伪影或需要手动参数调整的鲁棒性有限的影响。我们提出了 ROOF（面向稳健性的最佳分解），这是一种半盲框架，它将基于校准的建模与数据驱动的光谱分解相结合。它将串扰校正公式化为对角归一化非负矩阵分解问题，并通过从单标记控制样本获得的参考串扰矩阵进行正则化。正则化参数通过最大似然自动估计，消除了手动调整，同时适应样本特定的变化。结果 对合成和真实四波段荧光图像的实验表明，ROOF 始终优于最先进的串扰校正方法。 ROOF 实现了更高的校正精度，抑制过度校正伪影，保留具有生物学意义的荧光共定位，并且计算效率高。这些结果凸显了 ROOF 在可靠定量荧光成像方面的稳健性、效率和实用价值。可用性和实施​​代码可在 https://github.com/baobabking/ROOF 获取

papers.title: A Topology-Feature Disentangled Deep Clustering Method for scRNA-seq Based on Graph-to-MLP Distillation
papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Graph neural networks (GNNs), owing to their ability to model topological relationships between cells, have gradually emerged as a mainstream approach in the clustering analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. However, their practical application still faces the following challenges: (1) excessive smoothing undermines cellular heterogeneity; (2) pre-constructed graphs introduce end-to-end dependencies; (3) large-scale cellular graph computations are computationally intensive. Results To fully utilise the expression profiles and topological information contained within scRNA-seq data and overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Graph-to-MLP (G2M) knowledge distillation method incorporating AdaBoost principles, and builds upon this to develop a graph-disentangled single-cell clustering framework—scAdaG2M. This framework utilises a GNN teacher model to learn higher-order topological relationships and local neighbourhood structures between cells on a cellular graph, whilst multiple lightweight MLP student models perform feature learning in an ungraphed setting. By combining this with an AdaBoost-style dynamic reweighting strategy, the framework enhances the model’s ability to characterise cells that are difficult to distinguish, cells with blurred boundaries, and potentially rare cell populations, thereby mitigating the dilution of cellular heterogeneity caused by over-smoothing. At the same time, this framework effectively decouples graph-based modelling from graph-free reasoning, reduces the end-to-end reliance on pre-constructed graphs, and significantly reduces the computational overhead associated with large-scale cellular graphs. Availability All datasets used in this study are publicly available. Detailed information about all the single-cell datasets analyzed in this paper is provided in Supplementary Table 1. The source code is available at https://github.com/gxl1110/scAdaG2M and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21512950
papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Graph neural networks (GNNs), owing to their ability to model topological relationships between cells, have gradually emerged as a mainstream approach in the clustering analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. However, their practical application still faces the following challenges: (1) excessive smoothing undermines cellular heterogeneity; (2) pre-constructed graphs introduce end-to-end dependencies; (3) large-scale cellular graph computations are computationally intensive.

RESULTS: To fully utilise the expression profiles and topological information contained within scRNA-seq data and overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Graph-to-MLP (G2M) knowledge distillation method incorporating AdaBoost principles, and builds upon this to develop a graph-disentangled single-cell clustering framework-scAdaG2M. This framework utilises a GNN teacher model to learn higher-order topological relationships and local neighbourhood structures between cells on a cellular graph, whilst multiple lightweight MLP student models perform feature learning in an ungraphed setting. By combining this with an AdaBoost-style dynamic reweighting strategy, the framework enhances the model's ability to characterise cells that are difficult to distinguish, cells with blurred boundaries, and potentially rare cell populations, thereby mitigating the dilution of cellular heterogeneity caused by over-smoothing. At the same time, this framework effectively decouples graph-based modelling from graph-free reasoning, reduces the end-to-end reliance on pre-constructed graphs, and significantly reduces the computational overhead associated with large-scale cellular graphs.

AVAILABILITY: All datasets used in this study are publicly available. Detailed information about all the single-cell datasets analyzed in this paper is provided in Supplementary Table 1. The source code is available at https://github.com/gxl1110/scAdaG2M and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21512950.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Graph neural networks (GNNs), owing to their ability to model topological relationships between cells, have gradually emerged as a mainstream approach in the clustering analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. However, their practical application still faces the following challenges: (1) excessive smoothing undermines cellular heterogeneity; (2) pre-constructed graphs introduce end-to-end dependencies; (3) large-scale cellular graph computations are computationally intensive.

RESULTS: To fully utilise the expression profiles and topological information contained within scRNA-seq data and overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Graph-to-MLP (G2M) knowledge distillation method incorporating AdaBoost principles, and builds upon this to develop a graph-disentangled single-cell clustering framework-scAdaG2M. This framework utilises a GNN teacher model to learn higher-order topological relationships and local neighbourhood structures between cells on a cellular graph, whilst multiple lightweight MLP student models perform feature learning in an ungraphed setting. By combining this with an AdaBoost-style dynamic reweighting strategy, the framework enhances the model's ability to characterise cells that are difficult to distinguish, cells with blurred boundaries, and potentially rare cell populations, thereby mitigating the dilution of cellular heterogeneity caused by over-smoothing. At the same time, this framework effectively decouples graph-based modelling from graph-free reasoning, reduces the end-to-end reliance on pre-constructed graphs, and significantly reduces the computational overhead associated with large-scale cellular graphs.

AVAILABILITY: All datasets used in this study are publicly available. Detailed information about all the single-cell datasets analyzed in this paper is provided in Supplementary Table 1. The source code is available at https://github.com/gxl1110/scAdaG2M and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21512950.

SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: Supplementary data are available at Bioinformatics online.

all_papers.title: ROOF: Robustness-Oriented Optimal Factorization for Fluorescence Crosstalk Correction
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Fluorescence bleed-through (spectral crosstalk) compromises the accuracy of signal interpretation, quantification, and visualization in multi-band fluorescence microscopy. Existing correction methods rely either on experimental calibration or blind spectral unmixing, but often suffer from limited robustness to biological variability, overcorrection artifacts, or the need for manual parameter tuning. We propose ROOF (Robustness-Oriented Optimal Factorization), a semi-blind framework that unifies calibration-based modeling with data-driven spectral unmixing. It formulates crosstalk correction as a diagonally normalized nonnegative matrix factorization problem regularized by a reference crosstalk matrix obtained from single-labeled control samples. The regularization parameter is estimated automatically via maximum likelihood, eliminating manual tuning while adapting to specimen-specific variations. Results Experiments on synthetic and real four-band fluorescence images demonstrate that ROOF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art crosstalk correction methods. ROOF achieves higher correction accuracy, suppresses overcorrection artifacts, preserves biologically meaningful fluorescence colocalization, and is computationally efficient. These results highlight ROOF’s robustness, efficiency, and practical value for reliable quantitative fluorescence imaging. Availability and implementation The codes are available at https://github.com/baobabking/ROOF with
all_papers.abstract:
MOTIVATION: Fluorescence bleed-through (spectral crosstalk) compromises the accuracy of signal interpretation, quantification, and visualization in multi-band fluorescence microscopy. Existing correction methods rely either on experimental calibration or blind spectral unmixing, but often suffer from limited robustness to biological variability, overcorrection artifacts, or the need for manual parameter tuning. We propose ROOF (Robustness-Oriented Optimal Factorization), a semi-blind framework that unifies calibration-based modeling with data-driven spectral unmixing. It formulates crosstalk correction as a diagonally normalized nonnegative matrix factorization problem regularized by a reference crosstalk matrix obtained from single-labeled control samples. The regularization parameter is estimated automatically via maximum likelihood, eliminating manual tuning while adapting to specimen-specific variations.

all_papers.llm_research_question_zh: 荧光渗透（光谱串扰）会影响多波段荧光显微镜中信号解释、定量和可视化的准确性。
llm_highlights_zh: 现有的校正方法依赖于实验校准或盲光谱分离，但通常会受到对生物变异性、过度校正伪影或需要手动参数调整的鲁棒性有限的影响。
我们提出了 ROOF（面向稳健性的最佳分解），这是一种半盲框架，它将基于校准的建模与数据驱动的光谱分解相结合。
它将串扰校正公式化为对角归一化非负矩阵分解问题，并通过从单标记控制样本获得的参考串扰矩阵进行正则化。
all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 荧光渗透（光谱串扰）会影响多波段荧光显微镜中信号解释、定量和可视化的准确性。现有的校正方法依赖于实验校准或盲光谱分离，但通常会受到对生物变异性、过度校正伪影或需要手动参数调整的鲁棒性有限的影响。我们提出了 ROOF（面向稳健性的最佳分解），这是一种半盲框架，它将基于校准的建模与数据驱动的光谱分解相结合。它将串扰校正公式化为对角归一化非负矩阵分解问题，并通过从单标记控制样本获得的参考串扰矩阵进行正则化。正则化参数通过最大似然自动估计，消除了手动调整，同时适应样本特定的变化。结果 对合成和真实四波段荧光图像的实验表明，ROOF 始终优于最先进的串扰校正方法。 ROOF 实现了更高的校正精度，抑制过度校正伪影，保留具有生物学意义的荧光共定位，并且计算效率高。这些结果凸显了 ROOF 在可靠定量荧光成像方面的稳健性、效率和实用价值。可用性和实施​​代码可在 https://github.com/baobabking/ROOF 获取

all_papers.primary_summary_raw:
MOTIVATION: Fluorescence bleed-through (spectral crosstalk) compromises the accuracy of signal interpretation, quantification, and visualization in multi-band fluorescence microscopy. Existing correction methods rely either on experimental calibration or blind spectral unmixing, but often suffer from limited robustness to biological variability, overcorrection artifacts, or the need for manual parameter tuning. We propose ROOF (Robustness-Oriented Optimal Factorization), a semi-blind framework that unifies calibration-based modeling with data-driven spectral unmixing. It formulates crosstalk correction as a diagonally normalized nonnegative matrix factorization problem regularized by a reference crosstalk matrix obtained from single-labeled control samples. The regularization parameter is estimated automatically via maximum likelihood, eliminating manual tuning while adapting to specimen-specific variations.

RESULTS: Experiments on synthetic and real four-band fluorescence images demonstrate that ROOF consistently outperforms state-of-the-art crosstalk correction methods. ROOF achieves higher correction accuracy, suppresses overcorrection artifacts, preserves biologically meaningful fluorescence colocalization, and is computationally efficient. These results highlight ROOF's robustness, efficiency, and practical value for reliable quantitative fluorescence imaging.

AVAILABILITY AND IMPLEMENTATION: The codes are available at https://github.com/baobabking/ROOF with DOI:10.5281/zenodo.21872937.

all_papers.title: A Topology-Feature Disentangled Deep Clustering Method for scRNA-seq Based on Graph-to-MLP Distillation
all_papers.summary: Abstract Motivation Graph neural networks (GNNs), owing to their ability to model topological relationships between cells, have gradually emerged as a mainstream approach in the clustering analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. However, their practical application still faces the following challenges: (1) excessive smoothing undermines cellular heterogeneity; (2) pre-constructed graphs introduce end-to-end dependencies; (3) large-scale cellular graph computations are computationally intensive. Results To fully utilise the expression profiles and topological information contained within scRNA-seq data and overcome these limitations, this paper proposes a Graph-to-MLP (G2M) knowledge distillation method incorporating AdaBoost principles, and builds upon this to develop a graph-disentangled single-cell clustering framework—scAdaG2M. This framework utilises a GNN teacher model to learn higher-order topological relationships and local neighbourhood structures between cells on a cellular graph, whilst multiple lightweight MLP student models perform feature learning in an ungraphed setting. By combining this with an AdaBoost-style dynamic reweighting strategy, the framework enhances the model’s ability to characterise cells that are difficult to distinguish, cells with blurred boundaries, and potentially rare cell populations, thereby mitigating the dilution of cellular heterogeneity caused by over-smoothing. At the same time, this framework effectively decouples graph-based modelling from graph-free reasoning, reduces the end-to-end reliance on pre-constructed graphs, and significantly reduces the computational overhead associated with large-scale cellular graphs. Availability All datasets used in this study are publicly available. Detailed information about all the single-cell datasets analyzed in this paper is provided in Supplementary Table 1. The source code is available at https://github.com/gxl1110/scAdaG2M and https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21512950

all_papers.llm_rss_summary_zh: 图神经网络（GNN）由于能够模拟细胞之间的拓扑关系，已逐渐成为单细胞 RNA 测序（scRNA-seq）数据聚类分析的主流方法。然而，它们的实际应用仍然面临以下挑战：（1）过度平滑破坏了细胞异质性（2）预构建图引入了端到端依赖关系（3）大规模细胞图计算是计算密集型的。结果为了充分利用scRNA-seq数据中包含的表达谱和拓扑信息并克服这些限制，本文提出了一种结合AdaBoost原理的图到MLP（G2M）知识蒸馏方法，并在此基础上开发了图解缠结的单细胞聚类框架——scAdaG2M。该框架利用 GNN 教师模型来学习细胞图上细胞之间的高阶拓扑关系和局部邻域结构，同时多个轻量级 MLP 学生模型在无图环境中执行特征学习。通过将其与 AdaBoost 式的动态重新加权策略相结合，该框架增强了模型表征难以区分的细胞、边界模糊的细胞以及潜在稀有细胞群的能力，从而减轻了过度平滑导致的细胞异质性稀释。同时，该框架有效地将基于图的建模与无图推理解耦，减少了对预构建图的端到端依赖，​​并显着减少了与大规模细胞图相关的计算开销。可用性 本研究中使用的所有数据集都是公开的。 补充表1提供了本文分析的所有单细胞数据集的详细信息。源代码可在https://github.com/gxl1110/scAdaG2M和https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21512950获取
